reply:
That changes it: Default Redis persistence loses writes on crash. RDB snapshots run every few minutes (configurable, but not per-write), and AOF with appendfsync everysec (the default for AOF mode) loses up to ~1 second of writes. Only appendfsync always gives you durability on every write—at the cost of performance.

Cost of being wrong: silent data loss. A write returns success to the client, but a crash before the next snapshot or fsync flushes it.
